intervals.quote: October  Expected energy was achieved at RCS.

beam_power.note: The J-PARC history page (2018 July) states: "Continuous operation with a beam power equivalent to 1 MW was succeeded at MLF" (the MLF is fed by the RCS). Cross-check: the facilities page states the MLF is driven by "3 GeV protons with a current of 333 micro-amps and a repetition rate of 25 Hz", and 3 GeV x 333 uA = 0.999 MW, i.e. 1 MW.
beam_power.quote: Continuous operation with a beam power equivalent to 1 MW was succeeded at MLF

summary.plain: A fast-cycling ring that takes protons from the linac up to 3 billion electronvolts 25 times a second, feeding both a neutron source and the main ring.
summary.technical: 3 GeV rapid-cycling synchrotron, about 350 m circumference, 25 Hz repetition, ~1 MW beam power to the Materials and Life Science Experimental Facility; injects into the main ring.
